skill.name: frontend-components
skill.description: Build reusable, composable UI components with single responsibilities, clear prop interfaces, proper state management, and minimal coupling. Use this skill when creating or editing React components (.tsx, .jsx files), when designing component APIs with props, when implementing component composition patterns, when managing local component state, when building shadcn/ui components, when creating shared UI components in resources/js/Components/, when implementing component documentation, or when refactoring large components into smaller, focused pieces.

security_audit.summary: Two external command findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code examples. The path traversal finding is confirmed because SKILL.md directs the assistant to load guidance through a ../../../ relative link outside the skill directory.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md references component guidance through a parent-directory traversal link.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced component standards inside the skill package, or inline the required guidance in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 uses markdown inline code to name .tsx and .jsx file extensions. It does not invoke a shell or create a command execution path.

Line 28 instructs the assistant to follow a ../../../ relative path outside the skill directory. That creates a cross-boundary file access risk for marketplace installs.

content.value_statement: Large frontend components are hard to reuse, test, and maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create focused React components with clear props and state boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of focused React components in .tsx and .jsx files.
Supports clear prop interfaces and TypeScript component types.
Encourages composition from smaller UI components.
Helps decide when to keep local state or lift state upward.
Applies reusable component practices for shadcn/ui and shared component folders.
limitations: The skill provides guidance, not a runnable component library.
It depends on project-specific standards that may not be included in the package.
It does not validate visual accessibility or browser behavior by itself.
It focuses on React-style components, not every frontend framework.

use_cases.title: Create Shared UI Components
use_cases.description: Use the skill to design reusable buttons, cards, modals, forms, and layout components with clear responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Refactor Large Components
use_cases.description: Use the skill to split monolithic React components into smaller components with focused APIs and clearer state ownership.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component APIs
use_cases.description: Use the skill to align prop naming, TypeScript types, and composition patterns across shared component directories.
use_cases.target_user: Tech leads and design system maintainers

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable React component for this UI need. Keep one responsibility, clear props, and simple local state.

prompt_templates.title: Review Component Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component API. Suggest clearer prop names, TypeScript types, and defaults while keeping the public interface small.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for Composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this large component into smaller React components. Preserve behavior and explain the new ownership boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Shared Component Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a shared component pattern for this feature. Include composition choices, state placement, file organization, and usage guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a reusable alert component for success, warning, and error messages.
output_examples.output: A focused alert component plan with variant props, accessible labels, composition notes, and suggested file placement.

output_examples.input: Refactor a large settings panel that mixes form fields, validation, and layout.
output_examples.output: A breakdown into form sections, field components, validation helpers, and parent state ownership recommendations.

output_examples.input: Review a shared card component used across dashboards.
output_examples.output: Specific prop API improvements, composition changes, and documentation points for consistent dashboard usage.

best_practices: Keep each component focused on one responsibility.
Prefer explicit prop interfaces over hidden coupling.
Document shared components with expected usage and boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not place unrelated layout, data fetching, and business logic in one component.
Do not expose broad props that leak internal implementation details.
Do not create shared components before reuse requirements are clear.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React-style component work, including TypeScript, JSX, TSX, and shadcn/ui patterns.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready components?
faq.answer: It can guide component structure and APIs, but teams must still test behavior, accessibility, and visual output.

faq.question: Does it replace a design system?
faq.answer: No. It helps apply component discipline within an existing design system or shared UI folder.

faq.question: Can it help with refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports splitting large components into smaller units with clearer state and prop boundaries.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: Authors should remove parent-directory traversal links and include required guidance inside the skill package.
